event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: The 2023-09-28 Copart (CPRT) Form 10-K places COVID-19 in the filing’s risk landscape, but only at a generic, forward-looking level. The company flags the pandemic as one of many ‘public-health issues’ that could disturb international operations or overall results, and the MD&A boiler-plate notes that forward-looking statements cover possible COVID-19 impacts. There is no quantified disclosure of past financial damage, nor any detailed discussion of supply-chain interruptions, labour shortages, or remote-work challenges. Consequently, the risk is presented as a continuing but largely contingent threat rather than an observed material impact. Given that the pandemic event is recent (≈3.5 years old) under the Time-Decay Principle, a moderate score is still warranted, yet the absence of specificity or metrics tempers severity. Overall, the COVID-19 risk appears acknowledged but not deeply analysed, suggesting a medium-level concern (roughly mid-single-digit scoring across snippets).
